title: Uploads fail with 403 after a security hardening ticket
intro: Since this morning, user avatar uploads fail. The app logs show '403 AuthorizationFailure: This request is not authorized to perform this operation.' from the storage account stwebprod001. The app's credentials haven't changed. A security ticket 'restrict public network access to storage' was closed at 08:30.

expected_commands: az storage account show --name stwebprod001 --query networkRuleSet
az storage account show -n stwebprod001 --query networkRuleSet
steps.hint: defaultAction and the allow lists decide which networks can reach the account.

steps.prompt: Deny by default, and only the office range is allowed. The app runs on vm-app-01 in snet-app, which isn't listed. Check whether snet-app (vnet-web-prod, rg-web-prod) has the Microsoft.Storage service endpoint.
expected_commands: az network vnet subnet show --resource-group rg-web-prod --vnet-name vnet-web-prod --name snet-app --query serviceEndpoints
az network vnet subnet show -g rg-web-prod --vnet-name vnet-web-prod -n snet-app --query serviceEndpoints
steps.hint: A VNet rule on a storage account requires the subnet to have the Microsoft.Storage service endpoint.

steps.prompt: Enable the Microsoft.Storage service endpoint on snet-app.
expected_commands: az network vnet subnet update --resource-group rg-web-prod --vnet-name vnet-web-prod --name snet-app --service-endpoints Microsoft.Storage
az network vnet subnet update -g rg-web-prod --vnet-name vnet-web-prod -n snet-app --service-endpoints Microsoft.Storage
az storage account network-rule add --resource-group rg-web-prod --account-name stwebprod001 --vnet-name vnet-web-prod --subnet snet-app
az storage account network-rule add -g rg-web-prod --account-name stwebprod001 --vnet-name vnet-web-prod --subnet snet-app

steps.prompt: Test from the app VM itself: use Run Command on vm-app-01 (rg-web-prod) to check which address stwebprod001.blob.core.windows.net resolves to.
expected_commands: az vm run-command invoke --resource-group rg-web-prod --name vm-app-01 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "nslookup stwebprod001.blob.core.windows.net"
az vm run-command invoke -g rg-web-prod -n vm-app-01 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts 'nslookup stwebprod001.blob.core.windows.net'
steps.fake_output:
[stdout]
Name:    blob.ams07prdstr02a.store.core.windows.net
Address: 20.60.222.4
Aliases: stwebprod001.blob.core.windows.net
(uploads succeed again: the traffic arrives tagged with snet-app's service endpoint)
steps.hint: Run Command runs a script on the VM without SSH.

resolution: The hardening itself was right: flipping the storage account's default action to Deny cut it off from the whole internet. But the ticket was done in the wrong order and only accounted for the office. The app reaches storage from snet-app, which had neither a service endpoint nor an allow rule, so its requests were refused with an AuthorizationFailure 403, easily mistaken for a credentials problem. The order that avoids the outage: inventory the real clients first (the storage account's diagnostic logs show caller IPs), add their allow rules, and only then flip the default to Deny. A private endpoint is stronger than service endpoints: the account gets a private IP in the VNet and public access can be disabled entirely, but DNS must resolve to that private IP (privatelink.blob.core.windows.net), a classic follow-up mistake. The last step checks resolution for exactly that reason.
real_commands_used: az network vnet subnet show --query serviceEndpoints
